title: Backup & Safe File Recovery
purpose: Eight connected manual recovery exercises. Choose any lesson; the recommended sequence builds an evidence-based recovery workflow.
prerequisites: Bash quoting, files/permissions, disposable-user administration; unchanged approved administrator image. Guest-only sudo where stated.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 103.3 partial tar/gzip; LPIC-2 v4.5 206.2 partial manual backup, integrity and restore. Not a complete backup syllabus; self-reviewed and unscored.

entries.description: State what must be recovered before making a backup.
objectives: LPIC-1 v5.0 103.3 partial; LPIC-2 v4.5 206.2 partial; permission skills reinforce 104.5
materials: Guest-only practice. Lessons are display-only; the application never executes this text. Start on a fresh lesson disk. Enter the small fixture lines manually; no shared clipboard is assumed.

Stop on any failed guard, account collision, unexpected member, link or existing destination. Never adopt someone else's fixture. Only trusted, locally created regular files are extracted here; this is not a safe untrusted-archive extraction tool.

Use only the declared /home/learner/ll-backup-N area, no parent paths or system configuration. Archives are at most 64 KiB; commands have a ten-second timeout plus one-second kill grace. Begin with at least 64 MiB guest free space; this check is not a storage quota.

Challenge fixture only:
w=/home/learner/ll-backup-1; test "$(id -un)" = learner && test ! -e "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && mkdir -m 0700 -- "$w" && cd -- "$w" && test "$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')" -ge 65536
guard() { test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-backup-1 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-backup-1 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && test -z "$(find . -type l -print -quit)"; }; guard
guard && mkdir -m 0700 source && printf 'alpha\n' > source/note.txt && printf 'bravo\n' > 'source/space name.txt' && chmod 0640 source/note.txt && chmod 0600 'source/space name.txt' && touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC' source/note.txt 'source/space name.txt'
observations: Exact inventory, two hashes, expected metadata and RPO/RTO assumptions.
questions: Which metadata matters to access? What would make this reference trustworthy?
limitations: Self-reviewed and unscored. Keep evidence before Reset: VM disks and guest reports are excluded from profile backups; Resume boots disk state, not RAM/jobs.

Tar listing proves readable headers/member names, not payload correctness. gzip -t checks stream integrity, not expected contents or authenticity. A checksum reference is useful only if independently trusted and preserved.

Compare restored bytes, exact members, modes, owner/group and timestamps to known expectations. No ACL/xattr, rsync, cpio, links, devices, sparse files, remote backup, tape or complete objective coverage. Guest root can override guest-side limits.
cleanup: cd -- /home/learner/ll-backup-1; guard() { test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-backup-1 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-backup-1 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && test -z "$(find . -type l -print -quit)"; }; guard; find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2 -printf '%y %p\n'. Stop if anything differs from your fixture; retain evidence and backups until recovery review is complete.

After that inspection, rm -- 'source/note.txt' 'source/space name.txt' 'requirements.txt' 'expected.sha256' 'expected.metadata'; rmdir -- source; cd -- /home/learner; rmdir -- /home/learner/ll-backup-1. Use no -r, -f, globs or parent paths. On repetition, absent items are already clean; inspect remaining exact items before removing them.
troubleshooting: Do not extract again into a nonempty destination; inspect and use a fresh, named destination.
Read command status and compare data/metadata, not just a successful listing. Missing members and wrong versions can be perfectly valid archives.
On interruption retain the partial archive separately, inspect it, and create a differently named backup. Do not overwrite originals or earlier backups.

entries.description: Recover a private file for its intended disposable user.

Challenge starting conditions only:
w=/home/learner/ll-backup-6; test "$(id -un)" = learner && test ! -e "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && mkdir -m 0700 -- "$w" && cd -- "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && test "$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')" -ge 65536
guard() { test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-backup-6 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-backup-6 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && test -z "$(find . -type l -print -quit)"; }; guard

guard && ! getent passwd ll-b6 && ! getent group ll-b6 && sudo useradd -M -U -s /usr/sbin/nologin ll-b6 && sudo passwd -S ll-b6
guard && test ! -e v1.tar && test ! -L v1.tar && chmod 0711 . source && sudo chown ll-b6:ll-b6 source/note.txt && sudo chmod 0600 source/note.txt && sudo timeout -k 1s 10s tar -cf v1.tar -C source -- note.txt && sudo chown learner:learner v1.tar && sudo chmod 0600 v1.tar && mkdir -m 0711 restore && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -xf v1.tar -C restore --no-same-owner --same-permissions
observations: Locked account, before/after actual identity reads, owner:group600 and matching payload.
Backup archives/references are mode600; restore the saved practice-shell umask after cleanup.
questions: What can root bypass? Why does no-login not prevent runuser -- cat?

Tar listing proves readable headers/member names, not payload correctness. gzip -t checks stream integrity, not expected contents or authenticity. A checksum reference is useful only if independently trusted and preserved.

Compare restored bytes, exact members, modes, owner/group and timestamps to known expectations. No ACL/xattr, rsync, cpio, links, devices, sparse files, remote backup, tape or complete objective coverage. Guest root can override guest-side limits.
